clue.text: DiMaggio periodically visited a villain

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals from the baseball player's surname

explanation.surface: Joe DiMaggio, the baseball star, now and then called on some bad character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of DiMaggio.
explanation.definitionFit: The schemer in Shakespeare's Othello is literature's archetypal treacherous villain.

clue.text: Fie! I intend to be devious and vague

indicators.note: devious means wandering from the straight path, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust from someone planning to be sly and evasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be devious' rearranges FIE + IINTEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indefinite is unclear or not precisely fixed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: If you want to see a doctor with very little time, you'll need to hurry up

parts.note: to see something is to get it, as in understanding
MO, medical officer, is a doctor, with A as written
an eon is an age; calling it a little time is the setter's tongue-in-cheek understatement

explanation.surface: Practical advice: if you want a quick appointment with a GP, you'd better be quick.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a common crossword doctor. 'Little time' for EON is ironic: an eon is immensely long.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a move on is an informal idiom meaning to hasten.

clue.text: Singers disturbed rector with his bit of skirt

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged
a bit of the word skirt is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rector is shaken up by his girlfriend — 'bit of skirt' being slang for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges RECTOR + HIS into CHORISTER; 'bit of skirt' adds S. 'Bit of skirt' is British slang for an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Choir members are singers, especially in church choirs.

clue.text: Husband with power to dominate Mrs Tiggy-Winkle?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy tables
an edge is an advantage, a power over an opponent
to hog is to take over or monopolise

explanation.surface: A wife-controlling husband, wittily named after the Beatrix Potter washerwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is the Beatrix Potter washerwoman character; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is a prickly spined animal, so she is an example.

clue.text: The limit of x:y, plus any number

parts.note: x:y is how a ratio between two quantities is written
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A piece of maths jargon: the limit of a ratio plus an arbitrary number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The limit' sounds like calculus, but it is a fixed allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance that caps what one may have, hence a limit.

clue.text: Agree on a starting point

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: to square with something is to agree or tally with it
a means one

explanation.surface: Two parties settling on where to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to square one means back to the beginning, so it names the origin.

clue.text: Topless German soprano showing boobs

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, a German man
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a bare-chested German singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'boobs' play on the risqué, but boobs here is a verb: makes mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To boob is British slang for blundering, so it matches making mistakes.

clue.text: A spring onion served up in Scooby Snacks

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cartoon dog's treats come with a scallion on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides OBYS; 'served up' reads it upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybo is a Scottish dialect word for a scallion, a young green onion.

clue.text: Ex-chancellor takes a stunner to the other place

parts.note: a KO, knockout, is a blow that stuns
MPs call the House of Lords the other place; HL abbreviates it

explanation.surface: A former chancellor is carried off to the Lords with a stunning beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Commons the House of Lords is called 'the other place'. Helmut Kohl was German Chancellor 1982–98.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl led West Germany and then unified Germany as its head of government.

clue.text: Detective races to get dictionary copied

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
the TT races are the motorbike Tourist Trophy on the Isle of Man
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A detective rushes off to fetch a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditto is to repeat or duplicate what was said, as the ditto mark does.

clue.text: Genuine rag and bone

parts.note: genuine means real or true
to rag someone is to tease, or rib, them

explanation.surface: The cry of the rag-and-bone man, who collected scrap, made to sound authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag-and-bone man was a British street dealer collecting old junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy calls each of the upper seven pairs of ribs attached to the sternum this, so it is a skeletal part.

clue.text: Final Molière play coming to China

indicators.note: play here means move loosely about, so the letters are given free movement into a new order

explanation.surface: The last play by Molière arrives in China on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the noun for the French dramatist's work but is the anagram signal; China is porcelain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of Chinese porcelain with a black ground, so it is a kind of china.

clue.text: Small rodent: part of school master's ball practice

parts.note: British schools are often divided into houses
M stands for master, as in MA
O is round like a ball
usage or practice is use

explanation.surface: A school master's ball-game drill, with a rodent somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools split pupils into houses that compete at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The common domestic species of mouse is a small rodent living around people.

clue.text: Wild tercels circling rat holes

indicators.note: circling means going round the following word
wild signals the letters run free into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Male hawks fly wildly about a rat's burrows.
explanation.walkthrough: A tercel is a male hawk; 'holes' looks like the rat's burrows but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Small craters are little pits or depressions, so they are holes in a surface.

clue.text: Case involving criminal, loved in the world of fiction

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around the other part

parts.note: nom., the nominative, is a grammatical case

indicators.note: criminal signals the letters are crooked, set wrong

explanation.surface: A legal case concerning a criminal's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is grammar, not the courtroom: the nominative is abbreviated nom.
explanation.definitionFit: The realm of novels and novelists is literary fiction as a whole.

clue.text: They hang around and rile others, hard to ignore unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately signals things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
to ignore means leave out the letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Annoying people who are, sadly, hard to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' drops H from RILEOTHERS; 'unfortunately' rearranges RILEOTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers who linger without purpose are people who hang around.

clue.text: Louise has broken my crayon

indicators.note: has broken into means getting inside

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
Lou is short for Louise

explanation.surface: A child complains that Louise snapped their crayon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive. 'has broken' means Lou breaks into COR.
explanation.definitionFit: Crayon as a verb means to tint with a coloured pencil or stick, a direct synonym.

clue.text: US author produces book about Austrian composer

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other part

parts.note: a tome is a large book
Hugo Wolf was an Austrian song composer

explanation.surface: An American writer publishes a study of an Austrian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of The Bonfire of the Vanities was an American novelist and journalist.

clue.text: Subject of discussion ending with interior lines in circle

indicators.note: to line is to fill the inside, so the letter is set inside the subject

parts.note: a topic is a subject under discussion

indicators.note: ending with points to the final letter of interior

explanation.surface: A discussion topic ends up with geometry about lines inside a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending with interior' gives R, which 'lines' the inside of TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn mark parallels of latitude, each a circle round the globe.

clue.text: Unexpected meteor showers completely gutted part of England

indicators.note: unexpected suggests letters turning up in a surprising order
completely gutted removes all the inner letters, leaving just the outside pair

explanation.surface: Surprise meteor showers have left a county devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely gutted' leaves SS from showers; 'Unexpected' rearranges METEOR + SS. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This west-country county is a region of England.

clue.text: Woman is in hairdressers having top clipped

indicators.note: in places one part within another
clipping the top removes the opening letter, fitting for a down entry and a haircut

parts.note: a salon is a hairdresser's shop

explanation.surface: A woman is at the hairdresser's having her hair trimmed on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having top clipped' sounds like a haircut but removes the first letter of the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Singer in colourful clobber

parts.note: yellow is a colour
to clobber is to hit hard, to hammer

explanation.surface: A performer dressed in bright clothes — clobber being British slang for gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird; 'clobber' is a verb, not British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird is a bunting, and birds are singers in crosswordland.

clue.text: A Greek character joins southern alliance

parts.note: xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek joins a southern coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the WWII alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, so the word means a bloc.

clue.text: Intake of breath when visiting doctor

indicators.note: visiting means going inside the other part

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as means when, as in as he left

explanation.surface: A sharp breath taken during a trip to the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp inhalation, from shock or effort, is a breath drawn in.

clue.text: A dead duck cut in half — using this?

definitions.text: A dead duck cut in half — using this?

parts.note: D abbreviates dead, as in genealogies

indicators.note: cut in half keeps only the front half of the word

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what tool would split a dead duck down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nought in cricket; half of ZERO is ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: This chopping tool, like an axe with an arched blade, could cut a carcass in two.

clue.text: A speech delivered in 10 Downing Street?

definitions.meaning: a formal speech to an audience
a street location where mail is sent, here the Prime Minister's residence

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister speaks from inside Number 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Downing Street is the UK Prime Minister's residence; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal oration and the location details of a building.

clue.text: Ease with which Melissa regularly falls into temptation

indicators.note: falls into means dropping inside the other part

parts.note: a lure is a temptation

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: How easily Melissa keeps giving in to temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EIS from Melissa, which 'falls into' LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time spent at rest is relaxation, so the two words share the sense of repose.

clue.text: Parents wandering round meadow? What could be nicer?

indicators.note: round means surrounding the other part
wandering signals the letters roam into a new order

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad strolling through a field: what could be lovelier?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of Parents is PSANTER; lea is a poetic meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for agreeable is a synonym for more agreeable.

clue.text: What's in the centre of Skopje? Tsetse flies

indicators.note: in the centre of says the letters sit in the middle of the two place and insect words

explanation.surface: A quiz question about North Macedonia's capital, answered by an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like the insects, but it is a verb meaning travels by air.
explanation.definitionFit: To jet is to travel by aircraft, so it is a synonym for flies.
